'''Olaf Lechtenfeld''' is a German mathematical physicist, academic and researcher. He is a full professor at the Institute of [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] at [[Leibniz University Hannover|Leibniz University]], where he founded the Riemann Center for Geometry and Physics.<ref name=ITP>{{Cite web|url=https://www.itp.uni-hannover.de/de/ag/lechtenf/?&L=1|title=Olaf Lechtenfeld – Institute of Theoretical Physics – Leibniz University Hannover|website=Leibniz Universität Hannover|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref>

Lechtenfeld's research is focused on [[string theory]], [[gauge theory]] and [[Integrable system|integrable models]]. He has published over 200 research papers on [[mathematical physics]], classical and [[quantum field theory]], gravitation, [[supersymmetry]] and integrable many-body systems.<ref>{{Google scholar id|fwrBs0wAAAAJ}}</ref>

Lechtenfeld has a second career in amateur sports. He finished 25 marathons and numerous [[triathlon]]s (including 11 ironman races) and twice competed in the [[Ironman World Championship]] at [[Hawaiʻi]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ladv.de/leistungsdatenbank/athletenprofil/40364/Olaf-Lechtenfeld.htm|title=Olaf Lechtenfeld - TSV Victoria Linden|website=ladv.de|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://olaf-lechtenfeld.de/Vita/ironman.pdf|title=Ironman Olaf Lechtenfeld|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref>

== Education ==
Lechtenfeld was a student of physics and mathematics at [[University of Bonn]]. He completed his Diploma degree in 1982 and received his doctoral degree in 1984 from the university.<ref name=ITP/>

== Career ==
After his Ph.D., Lechtenfeld became a Research Fellow at [[CERN]] from 1985 till 1987. Lechtenfeld then took up the position of a research associate at [[City College of New York]] till 1990. For the subsequent two years, he was a Member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]]. In 1992, he moved from the US back to Germany and was appointed by the [[Leibniz University Hannover|University of Hannover]] (later renamed Leibniz University) as a professor of theoretical physics.<ref name=ITP/>

Lechtenfeld also held administrative appointments. He served as the founding dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at the university from 2005 till 2007. Between 2007 and 2014, Lechtenfeld was responsible for the Research Area "Space-Time" as a PI at the Cluster of Excellence QUEST.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/projekt/38928778?language=en|title=DFG - GEPRIS - EXC 201: QUEST - Centre for Quantum Engineering and Space-Time Research|website=gepris.dfg.de|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> From 2011 till 2018, he headed the Riemann Center for Geometry and Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rc.uni-hannover.de/en/center/people/members/|title=Members – Riemann Center for Geometry and Physics – RC|website=Leibniz Universität Hannover|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> Since 1995 he runs the annual Saalburg Summer School on Foundations and New Methods in Theoretical Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://saalburg.aei.mpg.de/|title=W.E. Heraeus Summer School "Saalburg" – for Graduate Students – on "Foundations and New Methods in Theoretical Physics"|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref>

== Research ==
Lechtenfeld has worked on mathematical physics, classical and quantum field theory, gravitation, supersymmetry and integrable many-body systems. A significant part of his research is focused on string theory.

=== Finite groups, mean fields, and supersymmetry ===
Lechtenfeld started his research in the early 1980s, with the representation theory of finite subgroups of SU(n). After obtaining his physics degree for introducing optimized mean fields for atoms, he discovered during his PhD a systematic construction of the Nicolai map for globally supersymmetric field theories. This allowed for its perturbative diagrammatic computation and established the existence of stochastic variables in certain theories.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0550321386905316|title=Stochastic variables in ten dimensions?|year=1986|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(86)90531-6|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=O.|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=274|issue=3–4|pages=633–652|bibcode=1986NuPhB.274..633L|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

35 years later, Lechtenfeld returned to the Nicolai map for supersymmetric [[Yang–Mills theory]] with an extension to all critical dimensions and an explicit complete evaluation to third order in the coupling.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Perturbative linearization of supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory|arxiv=2005.12324|last1=Ananth|first1=Sudarshan|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Malcha|first3=Hannes|last4=Nicolai|first4=Hermann|last5=Pandey|first5=Chetan|last6=Pant|first6=Saurabh|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|year=2020|volume=2020|issue=10|page=199|doi=10.1007/JHEP10(2020)199|bibcode=2020JHEP...10..199A|s2cid=218889791}}</ref>

=== String theory ===
Lechtenfeld has conducted significant research in string theory; after his Ph.D. he started working on this and related research areas in the second half of the 1980s. As a postdoc at CERN, Lechtenfeld developed conformal field methods for the computation of superstring scattering amplitudes, refining the bosonized vertex operator construction and applying it to four- and six-fermion scattering.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0550321387902136|title=Conformal techniques, bosonization and tree-level string amplitudes|year=1987|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(87)90213-6|last1=Alan Kostelecký|first1=V.|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Lerche|first3=Wolfgang|last4=Samuel|first4=Stuart|last5=Watamura|first5=Satoshi|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=288|pages=173–232|bibcode=1987NuPhB.288..173A|url-access=subscription}}</ref> After moving to the City College of New York, he pushed this approach to higher loops, including bosonization on higher-genus [[Riemann surface]]s. In particular, he found a new fermionic representation of beta-gamma systems by employing Fay's trisecant identity.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269389916869|title=Superconformal ghost correlations on Riemann surfaces|year=1989|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(89)91686-9|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=232|issue=2|pages=193–198|bibcode=1989PhLB..232..193L|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He also developed off-shell conformal methods for superstring field theory. Lechtenfeld then worked on [[random matrix]] models of two-dimensional [[quantum gravity]], a topic he continued during his membership at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. He applied the semiclassical approach to finite-N matrix models and derived an [[integral equation]] for the classical [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors|eigenvalue]] density.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Semiclassical Approach to Finite-N Matrix Models|year=1992|doi=10.1142/S0217751X92003264|arxiv=hep-th/9112045|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|journal=International Journal of Modern Physics A|volume=07|issue=28|pages=7097–7118|bibcode=1992IJMPA...7.7097L|s2cid=11025923}}</ref>

After accepting a full professorship in Hannover, Lechtenfeld focused his research to N=2 fermionic strings in 2+2 spacetime at tree and loop level. He worked out its path-integral quantization, BRST cohomology, nonlocal hidden symmetries and resulting stringy extensions of selfdual Yang–Mills theory and gravity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/512825|title=INSPIRE|website=inspirehep.net|access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> During the early 2000s, Lechtenfeld researched on superstring field theory, twistor string theory, topological and pure-spinor strings. He obtained exact solutions to Berkovits' [[string field theory]] and combined the Lorentz invariant N=2 string field theory with the twistor description of selfdual Yang–Mills theory.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269304011499|title=Supertwistors and cubic string field theory for open N=2 strings|journal = Physics Letters B|date = 23 September 2004|volume = 598|issue = 1–2|pages = 113–120|doi = 10.1016/j.physletb.2004.08.008|s2cid = 15062455|arxiv = hep-th/0406179|last1 = Lechtenfeld|first1 = Olaf|last2 = Popov|first2 = Alexander D.|bibcode = 2004PhLB..598..113L}}</ref>

Between 2007 and 2014, Lechtenfeld investigated heterotic string compactifications with fluxes and fermionic condensates on nearly [[Kähler manifold|Kähler]], [[G2 manifold|G2]] and [[Sasakian manifold]]s, to order α', finding families of non-supersymmetric string vacua.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Nearly Kähler heterotic compactifications with fermion condensates|year=2012|doi=10.1007/JHEP04(2012)114|arxiv=1202.1278|last1=Chatzistavrakidis|first1=Athanasios|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Popov|first3=Alexander D.|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2012|issue=4|page=114|bibcode=2012JHEP...04..114C|s2cid=119745850}}</ref>

=== Baryon number violation, hairy black holes, Gribov problem ===
In 1990, Lechtenfeld authored an article studying [[baryon number]] violation in the [[Standard Model]] at high temperature. His research indicated a negligible baryon number violation in high energy scattering.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/055032139090195J|title=Baryon number violation at high temperature in the standard model|year=1990|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(90)90195-J|last1=Dine|first1=Michael|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Sakita|first3=Bunji|last4=Fischler|first4=Willy|last5=Polchinski|first5=Joseph|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=342|issue=2|pages=381–408|bibcode=1990NuPhB.342..381D|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Between 1992 and 1996, Lechtenfeld occasionally worked on black holes with minimally coupled scalar hair in two and four dimensions. He constructed a partially analytic and a fully analytic solution representing deformations of the Schwarzschild black hole by a self-interacting scalar field; albeit violating the dominant energy condition. He also developed in general the linear perturbation theory for the stability of such backgrounds.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Scalar Deformations of Schwarzschild Holes and Their Stability|year=1998|doi=10.1142/S0217751X98000329|arxiv=gr-qc/9612062|last1=Dennhardt|first1=Helge|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|journal=International Journal of Modern Physics A|volume=13|issue=5|pages=741–764|bibcode=1998IJMPA..13..741D|s2cid=3110610}}</ref>

In 2013, Lechtenfeld found an explicit form for the Jacobian of arbitrary field-dependent BRST transformations in Yang–Mills theory. He showed that such transformations amount to a change of gauge and presented a formula for the BRST transformation producing any desired gauging.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269313005856|title=Field-dependent BRST transformations in Yang–Mills theory|year=2013|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2013.07.023|last1=Lavrov|first1=Peter M.|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=725|issue=4–5|pages=382–385|s2cid=118416853|arxiv=1305.0712|bibcode=2013PhLB..725..382L}}</ref> In an application to the Gribov copy problem, the Gribov–Zwanziger model was generalized beyond the [[Landau gauge]].

=== Noncommutative field theory ===
From 2001, Lechtenfeld conducted a decade-long analysis of Moyal-deformed field theories, with emphasis on its classical solutions such as noncommutative solitons, waves, vortices, baby Skyrmions, monopoles and instantons.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Noncommutative Solitons|doi=10.1142/9789812779649_0009|arxiv=hep-th/0605034|title=Noncommutative Geometry and Physics 2005|year=2007|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|pages=175–200|isbn=978-981-270-469-6|s2cid=119101522}}</ref> In particular, the construction of multi-solitons in Ward's modified [[sigma model]] and in the sine-Gordon model demonstrated the compatibility of Moyal deformations and integrability.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Noncommutative multi-solitons in 2+1 dimensions|year=2001|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2001/11/040|arxiv=hep-th/0106213|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|last2=Popov|first2=Alexander D.|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2001|issue=11|page=040|bibcode=2001JHEP...11..040L|s2cid=15514770|doi-access=free}}</ref> Lechtenfeld extended the analysis to supersymmetric models with non-anticommutative solitons and to the moduli-space (or adiabatic) dynamics of Moyal-deformed abelian sigma-model solitons.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Moduli-Space Dynamics of Noncommutative Abelian Sigma-Model Solitons|year=2006|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2006/06/028|arxiv=hep-th/0604219|last1=Klawunn|first1=Michael|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Petersen|first3=Stefan|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2006|issue=6|page=028|bibcode=2006JHEP...06..028K|s2cid=15710429}}</ref> He adapted the dressing, splitting and ADHM approaches to constructing noncommutative instantons<ref>{{cite journal|title=Noncommutative Instantons via Dressing and Splitting Approaches|year=2002|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2002/12/060|arxiv=hep-th/0211041|last1=Horváth|first1=Zalán|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Wolf|first3=Martin|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2002|issue=12|page=060|bibcode=2002JHEP...12..060H|s2cid=7875640}}</ref> and solved the [[Riemann–Hilbert problem]] for Moyal-deformed Wu–Yang, Dirac and BPS monopoles.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Noncommutative monopoles and Riemann-Hilbert problems|year=2004|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2004/01/069 |arxiv=hep-th/0306263|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|last2=Popov|first2=Alexander D.|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2004|issue=1|page=069|bibcode=2004JHEP...01..069L|s2cid=373515|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Integrable many-body systems ===
In 2003, Lechtenfeld started a new research line with extended supersymmetric mechanics and integrable many-body systems of Calogero–Moser type.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Superconformal mechanics|year=2012|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/45/17/173001|arxiv=1112.1947|last1=Fedoruk|first1=Sergey|last2=Ivanov|first2=Evgeny|last3=Lechtenfeld|first3=Olaf|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=45|issue=17|article-number=173001|bibcode=2012JPhA...45q3001F|s2cid=119153414}}</ref> He related N=4 superconformal multi-particle quantum mechanics to the celebrated WDVV equations and constructed a variety of novel models with D(2,1;α) superconformal invariance, some with extra spin variables.<ref>{{cite journal|title= N=4 Multi-Particle Mechanics, WDVV Equation and Roots|year = 2011|doi = 10.3842/SIGMA.2011.023|arxiv = 1011.2207|last1 = Lechtenfeld|first1 = Olaf|last2 = Schwerdtfeger|first2 = Konrad|last3 = Thürigen|first3 = Johannes|journal = Symmetry, Integrability and Geometry: Methods and Applications|volume = 7|page = 023|bibcode = 2011SIGMA...7..023L|s2cid = 975562}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Many-particle mechanics with D(2,1;alpha) superconformal symmetry|year=2011|doi=10.1007/JHEP02(2011)042|arxiv=1012.4639|last1=Krivonos|first1=Sergey|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|volume=2011|issue=2|page=042|bibcode=2011JHEP...02..042K|s2cid=119301659}}</ref> He reduced integrable superconformal mechanics to its angular sector and found the hidden symmetries and conserved charges of the latter.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Invariants of the spherical sector in conformal mechanics|year=2011|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/44/5/055205|arxiv=1008.2912|last1=Hakobyan|first1=Tigran|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Nersessian|first3=Armen|last4=Saghatelian|first4=Armen|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=44|issue=5|article-number=055205|bibcode=2011JPhA...44e5205H|s2cid=119640406}}</ref> For the quantum angular Calogero–Moser models Lechtenfeld calculated the energy spectra and eigenstates, the conserved charges and intertwiners, and the admissible PT deformations.<ref>{{cite journal|title= The quantum angular Calogero-Moser model|year= 2013|doi= 10.1007/JHEP07(2013)162|arxiv= 1305.5841|last1= Feigin|first1= Mikhail|last2= Lechtenfeld|first2= Olaf|last3= Polychronakos|first3= Alexios P.|journal= Journal of High Energy Physics|volume= 2013|issue= 7|page= 162|bibcode= 2013JHEP...07..162F|s2cid= 55552279}}</ref> For the rational and trigonometric models he also described the algebra of the conserved charges and revealed a nonlinear supersymmetry for integral couplings.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Nonlinear supersymmetry in the quantum Calogero model|year= 2014|doi= 10.1007/JHEP04(2014)151|arxiv= 1312.5749|last1= Correa|first1= Francisco|last2= Lechtenfeld|first2= Olaf|last3= Plyushchay|first3= Mikhail|journal= Journal of High Energy Physics|volume= 2014|issue= 4|page= 151|bibcode= 2014JHEP...04..151C|s2cid= 12509832}}</ref>

In 2017 he proposed a curved-space generalization of the WDVV equations and the related N=4 supersymmetric mechanics. In 2018, Lechtenfeld formulated Calogero–Moser models with an arbitrary number of supersymmetries by increasing the number of fermionic degrees of freedom to the square of the bosonic ones.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269318305744|title=N-extended supersymmetric Calogero models|year=2018|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2018.07.036|last1=Krivonos|first1=Sergey|last2=Lechtenfeld|first2=Olaf|last3=Sutulin|first3=Anton|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=784|pages=137–441|arxiv=1812.10168|bibcode=2018PhLB..784..137K|s2cid=73535014}}</ref>

=== Yang–Mills fields in higher dimensions and electromagnetic knots ===
In 2006 Lechtenfeld began investigating the equivariant coset-space [[dimensional reduction]] of Yang–Mills theories, which led to new types of quiver gauge theory and its vortex solutions. He constructed [[instanton]] solutions on coset manifolds and cones thereover with special holonomy and extended them to flux vacua of the heterotic string.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Yang-Mills Flows on Nearly Kähler Manifolds and G 2-Instantons|year=2010|doi=10.1007/s00220-010-1115-7|arxiv=0909.2730|last1=Harland|first1=Derek|last2=Ivanova|first2=Tatiana A.|last3=Lechtenfeld|first3=Olaf|last4=Popov|first4=Alexander D.|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=300|issue=1|pages=185–204|bibcode=2010CMaPh.300..185H|s2cid=17074395}}</ref>

After 2014 adiabatic limits of Yang–Mills theory on warped product spaces became a subject of Lechtenfeld's research. He showed that in certain infrared limits the moduli-space approximation leads to Skyrme or Faddeev or even superstring sigma models.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Skyrme and Faddeev models in the low-energy limit of 4d Yang-Mills-Higgs theories|year=2019|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2019.114675|arxiv=1808.08972|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|last2=Popov|first2=Alexander D.|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=945|article-number=114675|bibcode=2019NuPhB.94514675L|s2cid=119595870}}</ref>

In 2017, Lechtenfeld reconstructed exact finite-action Yang–Mills solutions on four-dimensional [[De Sitter space|de Sitter]] and [[Anti-de Sitter space|anti de Sitter spaces]] by reducing the problem to the Newtonian mechanics of a particle moving in R^3 subject to a quartic potential.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Solutions to Yang-Mills equations on four-dimensional de Sitter space|year= 2017|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.061601|arxiv= 1704.07456|last1= Ivanova|first1= Tatiana A.|last2= Lechtenfeld|first2= Olaf|last3= Popov|first3= Alexander D.|journal= Physical Review Letters|volume= 119|issue= 6|article-number= 061601|pmid= 28949611|bibcode= 2017PhRvL.119f1601I|s2cid= 206296288}}</ref> The discovery of Abelian configurations led Lechtenfeld to a novel construction method for all rational vacuum Maxwell solutions (so-called electromagnetic knots) in [[Minkowski space]], which exploits a hidden O(4) symmetry.<ref>{{cite journal|title=A new construction of rational electromagnetic knots|year=2018|doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2018.04.027|arxiv=1711.11144|last1=Lechtenfeld|first1=Olaf|last2=Zhilin|first2=Gleb|journal=Physics Letters A|volume=382|issue=23|pages=1528–1533|bibcode=2018PhLA..382.1528L|s2cid=119586198}}</ref>
